_comment: Edit this, then run generate_keymap.py and reflash. `layers` is a list of up to 4 macro layers -- hold A and B together (no need to also hold the info key) to cycle to the next one. Each layer's `keys` maps A-E to a short 'name' (shown on the OLED peek screen) and a list of 'actions'. A key can be omitted from a layer entirely if that layer has no use for it -- it'll just do nothing there. An action starting with 'TAP:' sends that QMK keycode (e.g. 'TAP:LCTL(KC_C)', 'TAP:KC_ENTER'); anything else is typed out literally as text.
